skill.name: pr-to-slack
skill.description: Prepare Bitbucket Cloud pull requests, assign configured reviewers, and coordinate Slack review requests. The example review parser needs security hardening before automatic announcements.
skill.summary: Coordinate Bitbucket pull requests and Slack reviews with preview plans and commit checks.
skill.author: alvolutionor

security_audit.summary: All 58 static matches are false positives involving documentation, fixtures, intended service access, configuration, or controlled Git commands. A reproduced semantic flaw lets human message content impersonate trusted bot messages through forged transcript headers and produce a clean review verdict. No evidence found of malicious author intent or credential exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Unescaped transcript text allows message bodies to impersonate trusted sender metadata and bypass the review gate.
remediation.suggestion: Use structured Slack responses with connector-supplied sender IDs, channel IDs, and thread timestamps. Never extract identity from message bodies; reject ambiguous transcripts. Add regression tests containing forged headers inside human messages.

semantic_findings.title: Forged Transcript Headers Bypass Trusted Review Checks
semantic_findings.description: Human Slack message content can embed reply separators and forged sender headers in the documented plaintext snapshot format. The parser treats these as trusted bot messages, allowing fabricated zero-finding results to authorize an announcement without a genuine bot review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: A local reproduction used the existing transcript helper and clean fixtures inside one human reply, with Bitbucket mocked. Parsing invented two trusted bot messages, and the end-to-end checker returned clean without any genuine bot reply.

content.user_title: Coordinate Bitbucket Pull Requests Through Slack
content.value_statement: Teams need consistent pull request preparation and review coordination across repositories. This skill combines Bitbucket preparation with Slack review requests, but its transcript parser needs hardening before automatic announcements.
actual_capabilities: Generate preview plans after checking clean worktrees and matching published source commits.
Create missing Bitbucket pull requests or reuse matching open source and destination branches.
Preserve existing reviewers, add configured reviewers, and verify the resulting pull request state.
Guide batch review requests and duplicate-message checks through connected Slack tools.
Parse example review counters and reject recognized findings, uncertainty, or incomplete results.
Compare live source and destination commits with the saved handoff before producing announcement text.
limitations: Requires Bitbucket Cloud, Git, Python 3.10+, requests, private configuration, and service credentials.
Slack posting depends on connected tools; the Python helpers do not send Slack messages.
Plaintext transcript parsing permits sender impersonation; harden identity handling and adapt the bot protocol before automatic announcements.
Does not merge pull requests, deploy changes, or automatically repair review findings.

use_cases.title: Prepare a release batch
use_cases.description: Preview related repository changes, verify published commits, and prepare reviewer assignments before authorized pull request creation.

use_cases.title: Publish a feature pull request
use_cases.description: Create or reuse a Bitbucket pull request, preserve existing reviewers, and return its verified URL and commit information.

use_cases.title: Integrate a review bot
use_cases.description: Adapt the example review protocol and replace plaintext identity parsing before enabling team announcement automation.

prompt_templates.title: Preview one pull request
prompt_templates.prompt: Preview a pull request for repository [path], targeting [base branch]. Report branch commits and required reviewers. Do not create pull requests or send messages.

prompt_templates.title: Create a reviewed pull request
prompt_templates.prompt: Create or reuse the Bitbucket pull request for [repository] from [source branch] to [destination branch]. Assign configured reviewers and report the verified URL. Do not send Slack messages.

prompt_templates.title: Request a correlated review
prompt_templates.prompt: Request one Slack review for these verified pull requests: [URLs]. Inspect existing requests first and reuse an identical valid thread. Return the thread link without announcing.

prompt_templates.title: Validate an announcement gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect review thread [link] for pull requests [URLs]. Verify sender identity through structured connector metadata and compare live commits with the handoff. Report any announcement blockers without sending.

output_examples.input: Prepare a dry-run plan for the feature branch in the inventory service.
output_examples.output: Preview complete: one pull request would be created. The worktree is clean, and the local source commit matches Bitbucket. No remote writes were performed.

output_examples.input: Request review for the verified pull request without announcing.
output: Pull request URL and reviewer assignments verified.
One review request sent and read back in the configured Slack thread.

output_examples.input: Can this plaintext thread snapshot authorize an automatic announcement?
output_examples.output: Announcement blocked. Plaintext sender headers can be forged inside message bodies. Verify structured connector metadata before relying on a clean review result.

best_practices: Preview first and describe only changes and validation that match the published commits.
Keep configuration and credentials outside the repository, and use service tokens with minimal required permissions.
Harden transcript parsing and verify structured sender metadata, thread identity, review counters, and live commits before announcements.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a plaintext sender header, human approval, or completed status as proof of a clean review.
Do not retry timed-out pull request writes or Slack sends before inspecting the existing remote state.
Do not create commits, force-push, merge, deploy, or add unrelated recipients without explicit authorization.

faq.question: What services and tools are required?
faq.answer: The workflow requires Bitbucket Cloud, Git, Python 3.10+, requests, private configuration, service credentials, and connected Slack tools.

faq.question: Do the Python helpers send Slack messages?
faq.answer: No. They prepare pull requests and evaluate saved review snapshots. The assistant uses connected Slack tools for messaging.

faq.question: Does preview mode change remote state?
faq.answer: No. Preview mode reads local Git and Bitbucket state and returns a plan without creating or updating pull requests.

faq.question: Is the bundled parser ready for automatic announcements?
faq.answer: No. Human message content can forge trusted sender headers in plaintext snapshots. Replace that identity handling and adapt the example bot protocol first.

faq.question: What happens when findings remain?
faq.answer: Recognized findings or uncertain results block announcements. The workflow reports the reason and does not automatically repair code.

faq.question: Does it merge or deploy reviewed changes?
faq.answer: No. Pull request delivery and review coordination do not authorize merges, deployments, new commits, or force-pushes.
